benchmark: crawl-budget-yield: how much of a page budget buys evidence, measured on one live catalogue crawl
site: scrapeme.live/shop (a public scraping-practice WooCommerce site), seed https://scrapeme.live/shop/, depth 2, max_pages 60, max_urls 120, ECDEV robots and pacing, query pokemon, force_refresh
yield_definition: pages_with_snapshot: leased URLs that were fetched and extracted; candidates: product candidates the run produced. Both are counts of what the budget bought, not a claim about completeness of the catalogue.
finding: In the first run 16 of 60 budgeted attempts (27%) were robots-denied add-to-cart URLs (?add-to-cart=N) answered from the cached robots.txt: no request was made, yet each used a page-budget unit and the origin interval. 5 more went to feed URLs that returned a non-HTML content type (UNSUPPORTED_CONTENT_TYPE).
fix: A refusal decided by policy before any request no longer spends the page budget or paces the origin (Frontier::fail_unspent, AcquireError::spent_no_request; the adapter also now reports the request count on robots refusals). Real attempts, retries and fetches that failed still count.
effect: same seed and limits: pages fetched and extracted 42 -> 55 (+31%), candidates 16 -> 19, network requests 43 -> 56 within the same budget of 60
yield_based_early_stopping: not adopted and not decidable on this trace: with 55 pages the run was still PARTIAL (32 URLs pending); yield per page was not flat enough to define a stopping point, and one practice site is not a defensible operating point. Remains an open BENCHMARK_CANDIDATE needing traces from several real catalogues.
limits: one site, one run before and one after; live pages and pacing vary run to run
a practice site whose robots.txt denies add-to-cart is the cleanest case; the size of the effect on other catalogues is unmeasured, though add-to-cart, sort, filter and login links are common
the before/after is a demonstration on the sample that exposed the defect, not independent proof
5 of 60 attempts in the second run still went to feed URLs; pre-filtering by extension was not adopted (an earlier measurement on Wikipedia showed extension filters would drop real HTML pages)
